etymology: Latin: argumentum ad lapidem - Dr Johnson refuted Berkeley by kicking a stone and saying “I refute it thus”.
committed_when: A claim sounds wrong on its face and the speaker cannot say why.
tell: The reply is a verdict - ridiculous, obviously false, come on - with no reason attached to it.
counter: Ask for the reason. If the claim really is absurd, the reason is easy to give, and giving it is the whole difference.
senses: Dismissing a claim as absurd without saying what is wrong with it, treating obviousness as an argument.
It works because most absurd-sounding claims are absurd, so the reflex is usually right. The problem is that it cannot tell the two cases apart, and it never has to show its work.
example: “That is the dumbest thing I have heard all week.” Possible. The sentence has not said which part is wrong.

confused_with.tell: Ridicule makes the claim funny; the stone simply declares it absurd. The stone is lazier and more common.
